forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For every real number x, x = floor(x) + frac(x), and 0 <= frac(x) < 1.

payload.previous_feedback: Previous vetter reason: The proof directly matches the lemma statement and is logically complete: it uses the definition of floor(x) as the greatest integer less than or equal to x, concludes floor(x) <= x, and then universally generalizes over arbitrary real x.
payload.previous_proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) itself is an integer that is less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for every real number x.
payload.role_in_assembly: Provides the basic lower floor bound used upstream to prove nonnegativity of x - floor(x).

payload.statement_nl: For every real number x, floor(x) ≤ x.

result_payload.addressed_previous_feedback: I made the key definition explicit and kept the universal quantification clear: for arbitrary real x, floor(x) is an integer ≤ x, so the inequality follows directly.
result_payload.proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number. By definition, floor(x) is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore floor(x) is itself an integer and satisfies floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the defining property of the floor function: floor(x) is an integer not exceeding x. Hence floor(x) ≤ x for all real x.
